comments.text:
You know what's worse than being ignorant? Being ignorant and oblivious. Know what you don't know! I find finance hard to understand but I know a few basic stuff:
1. No one will give you stuff without getting money. If a deal sounds too good to be true, it ISN'T TRUE!
2. For every "deal" there's always a catch
3. Avoid debt at all costs. If you can't afford something don't buy it. (Necessities are understandable if you have no choice but try to be frugal)
4. Money isn't infinite if you don't earn money
5. There's a big gap between cost and worth
6. Don't pay for something when you don't know what you are getting in return
7. Don't gamble. It rarely ends well (people waste too much money on the lottery)
8. Always consider added taxes and interest
9. Don't split payments and then forget about it. You're not getting off with a fraction of the cost. It'll bite you in the ass.
There is probably more I can't think of now.
2 things that surprised me in this vid: $200 for a train ticket? OMG! 😱 Now I know I'm not in the US and that train ride is longer but prices here are about...$10-$25 or so I think.
And do modifications really not add any value? That sounds crazy to me. I mean if the car is a piece of junk (I don't know cars) then a polished turd is still a turd but if it's reasonable, improving the engine, better wheels, sound system, sunroof, what-have-you should up the value. Of course no sane person would pay top dollar for a piece of crap with chrome wheels or something stupid like that.
We need to fix education! And it's not about throwing money at it. We need a reform. What matters is what's being taught and how. Throw out DEI BS and put in useful material like personal economics, critical thinking, the scientific method and basic science and math literacy (and comprehension!), how to search and verify information, global geography and historical context etc. Of course these are rights we have to fight for.
